definitions.meaning: a harmonica, a small instrument blown across the lips
the tongue is literally an organ found inside the mouth

explanation.surface: A harmonica player is told to put the instrument to their tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied to' links the two senses; the second reads the answer literally as an organ of the mouth, which the tongue is.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a blown instrument, and the tongue is a body part housed in the oral cavity.

clue.text: King of Naples raised old army: spirit

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
rum is a spirit made from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A monarch of Naples mustered a veteran force fortified by liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TA + RUM upwards into MURAT. Joachim Murat, Napoleon's marshal, was King of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Joachim Murat, Napoleon's brother-in-law, ruled the southern Italian kingdom from 1808 to 1815.

definitions.meaning: a position of control or superiority
a hand is a worker, and a foreman is the worker placed above the others

explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained by' links the senses. A 'hand' is a labourer, so the overseer is the higher one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dominance; a supervisor is the senior labourer, a 'hand' ranked higher.

clue.text: Inn has grand egg concoction, for a wonder !

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of the four words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A pub serves a fine egg dish that is a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' mixes the 14 letters of INN HAS GRAND EGG. The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
explanation.definitionFit: The terraced gardens of Babylon are listed among the seven marvels of antiquity.

clue.text: French dramatist is an odd sort also

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the word sort is put in a strange order

parts.note: and means also or in addition

explanation.surface: A French playwright is said to be a peculiar type of person, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges SORT into ROST. Edmond Rostand wrote 'Cyrano de Bergerac'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Rostand was the French playwright behind Cyrano de Bergerac.

clue.text: Children's author and' artist writes of a dry spring

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol, so dry
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A writer and illustrator for children produces work about a parched water source.
explanation.walkthrough: Mabel Lucie Attwell wrote and drew chubby-cheeked children's books. The grid prints ACTWELL, but A + TT + WELL spells her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel Lucie Attwell was an English illustrator who also wrote picture books for the young.

indicators.note: coming back tells us to read the golfing word from right to left

parts.note: in golf to top a drive is to hit the ball above centre, a bad shot, so drives badly is tops

explanation.surface: A golfer's poor tee shots leave a blemish on the scorecard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns TOPS round. Topping is a golfing fault: striking the top of the ball so it scuttles along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or stain.

parts.note: Tommy is the nickname of the British private soldier; the clue asks for the French equivalent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' (Tommy Atkins) was the British infantryman; his French counterpart in the First World War had a slang name meaning 'hairy one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War French infantryman was the counterpart of the British private.

definitions.meaning: H. M. ..., English novelist and travel writer
a Kipling ballad about a worldly man rejected by both Heaven and Hell

explanation.walkthrough: 'reads' links the two senses: H. M. Tomlinson wrote 'The Sea and the Jungle'; Kipling's poem of the same name is about a soul turned away at Heaven and Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a writer, H. M. Tomlinson, and a Kipling ballad carry this surname.

definitions.meaning: read literally: I am very gracious and good

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation of surprise, taken word by word, says the speaker is good and gracious.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cries of astonishment, and literally a boast of one's own graciousness.

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
pine trees grow needles instead of leaves, so they make needles

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the people who manufacture sewing needles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle-makers' suggests a factory, but it is trees: conifers produce needles.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, so it means being discontented.

clue.text: Element is an unusually hot one put in spirit

indicators.note: unusually tells us the word hot appears in an unusual order
put in means the numeral piece goes inside the drink word

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chemist describes an element as a strangely hot thing dissolved in liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes THO from HOT; 'put in' places I inside RUM, giving RIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorium is a radioactive metallic chemical element, number 90.

clue.text: Bound to call in before the tea-break

indicators.note: before places the first pieces ahead of the scrambled drink

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
taken as written

indicators.note: break, joined to tea, signals that the drink's letters are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to phone before the office's afternoon pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-break' looks like a single word for a rest, but 'break' rearranges TEA into ATE. 'Bound' is a verb here: to set a limit to.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound something is to set its limit or end, as to finish or conclude it.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the novelist's name is made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A book by the Victorian novelist Ouida is set in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Ouida was a Victorian novelist, so 'novel' poses as a book. Douai is a Catholic school in Berkshire, England, founded by monks from Douai in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Douai School was an English Benedictine boarding school.

definitions.meaning: in British usage to ... someone is to insult them

explanation.surface: Coarse speech is full of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two senses. As a verb, 'slang' means to hurl abuse at someone, mainly in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial vocabulary is informal speech; to berate someone verbally is a British verbal sense.

clue.text: A bit of a game appears to upset one, relatives conclude

indicators.note: conclude says the family word comes at the end of the run

parts.note: to spill a drink is to upset it
I is the Roman numeral one
kin are relatives or family

explanation.surface: A player gets upset in a game, and the family wind it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The page breaks 'conclude' over two lines as 'con-clude', which the text misread as 'con-elude'. A spillikin is one of the sticks in the game of spillikins, picked off a heap without disturbing the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillikin is one of the thin sticks used in the pick-up-sticks game.

clue.text: Wildly excited and irritated backer promises to pay

indicators.note: backer, read as more backward, tells us to turn the word for irritated round

parts.note: riled means irritated or annoyed
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: An investor, angry and holding IOUs, is beside himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backer' seems to be a financial sponsor, but it signals that RILED is read backwards as DELIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone delirious is frenzied or ecstatic, beside themselves with excitement.

parts.note: read as medical treatment, given too large a quantity of a drug

explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated generously' suggests kindness; medically it means given too much of a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given an excessive amount of a drug is medical treatment carried to excess.

parts.note: the poet's inkwell held what he wrote his poem about a Native American with: a black drawing ink named after a people of Asia

explanation.surface: The poet Longfellow dips his pen into his inkwell while composing his Native American epic.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow wrote 'The Song of Hiawatha' about an Ojibwe hero; the ink in his well is pictured as the ink of an 'Indian', though the name really refers to India.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense black ink fills the poet's well, and his subject was a Native American hero.

clue.text: Old Don Juan's confession ? That's laying it on thick !

definitions.meaning: an aged seducer admits '...', O being love, the tennis score of zero
the painting technique of applying thick layers

explanation.walkthrough: Split I'M PAST O, it is the ageing lover's admission that love (O, as in a tennis score) is behind him. As one word it is paint laid thickly on the canvas. 'That's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint applied heavily so brushstrokes stand out; the split reading is an elderly rake's admission.

clue.text: Connected with a Moscow philanthropist, perhaps?

parts.note: a philanthropist is kind, benevolent to others
a Red is a Soviet communist, associated with Moscow

explanation.surface: Someone has links with a generous benefactor in the Russian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A Moscow philanthropist is a 'kind Red', a benevolent communist. 'Connected' means related.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means related, linked by family or nature.

definitions.meaning: decent, without anything indecent or improper

explanation.walkthrough: In 'I clean forgot', the word means 'completely'; a joke without smut is also described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means utterly or entirely; as an adjective it describes decent, unsmutty material.

indicators.note: set-back means the letters picked are then read backwards
some means only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A ridiculous reversal of fortune is obvious to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes DICUL from inside 'ridiculous'; 'set-back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid writing is clear and easy to understand.

parts.note: a body journeying through space that trails a glowing tail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Space traveller' suggests an astronaut, but this one has a tail of gas and dust.
explanation.definitionFit: This icy body orbits the sun and grows a bright tail as it nears.

parts.note: read not as script but as the hand-held thing that grips a nib for writing

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'handwriting' so it can describe a holder you grip in the hand when writing.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is a holder held in the fingers into which a nib fits for writing.

parts.note: flight means a staircase, and one up is a single vertical board of a step

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft, but it is a flight of stairs; the vertical part of each step is this, and someone getting up is also one.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright board of a stair, between treads, rises in a staircase.

clue.text: Kipling's work soon set new fashion in Far Eastern wear.

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel about an orphan boy in India

indicators.note: set new fashion signals the letters of soon arranged in a fresh form

explanation.surface: Kipling's writing quickly launches a vogue for oriental clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set new fashion' rearranges SOON into ONOS after KIM, Kipling's 1901 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese robes with wide sleeves are traditional dress from that part of Asia.

definitions.meaning: ohms are the unit of electrical resistance, so adding ohms to a circuit does this to current

explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'Opposes—by insertion of OHMS?'; OHMS in capitals also suggests On Her Majesty's Service, but it is the electrical unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand is to oppose; an electrical component measured in ohms impedes current flow.

parts.note: any letter other than that single vowel; whole it is a short written message

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer says 'not E', so it covers every letter but one; it is also a word for a short letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written message, a short missive, is a form of letter.

clue.text: Worker of a modern sort turned revolutionary

indicators.note: sort as a verb means to arrange, so the two words are rearranged
turned tells us the political word is reversed

parts.note: a red is a communist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A labourer of the up-to-date kind has become a political radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges A MODERN into ROADMEN; 'turned' reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who repairs roads is a manual labourer.
